To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we measured the proton energy spectra from4He(γp)t breakup,4He(γ,ppn) and4He(γπ−p) reactions in the energy range Eγ =130−525 Mev.
the sum of the two-body breakup and the quasidisintegration channels resembles the free-nucleon cross sections when Fermi motion effects are included.
the sum of the two-body breakup and the quasfree pion production channels resembles the corresponding free-nucelon differential cross section when taking into account Fermi motion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the photodisintegration of4He in the energy region where theΔ(1232) resonance is present, using tagged photon energies up to 525 MeV and at an angle of Θlab=37.1o in the proton lab system.
the study of photoabsorption processes on the4He nucleus.
the study of the photoabsorption of photons on nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data do not contradict the assumption of a free nucleon structure of4He.
, at the present level of experimental precision, the data are in good agreement with theoretical expectations.
the present experimental results are well reproduced by a model which includes the quasifreepion production process, and which is based on the free-nucleon cross section.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data are consistent with a quasifree model, with the possible exception of the two-nuclear photon absorption channel at low energy, which shows a strong energy dependence.
the proton photoabsorption cross section of4He is dominated by two-nucleon absorption processes in the energy range of theΔ resonance.
the proton emission from4He is dominated by the quasifreepion production channel in the Δ-resonance region and that the2nγ channel is negligible in the present energy range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quasifreeze pion-production channel dominates the total reaction cross section in this region of excitation energy.
in this energy range the two-nucleonic processes are the dominant reaction channels.

the two-nucleons in4He are strongly bound and thus the two-nucleus photon absorption cross sections are much smaller than the corresponding free-nuclear cross sections, even in the region of theΔ(1232) resonance.
